explanation: Tipping, known locally as baksheesh, is deeply embedded in Egyptian service culture and meaningfully supplements low service wages. Restaurants commonly add a service charge (often around 12%) plus VAT to the bill, but a separate cash tip of around 10% directly to the server is still customary since the printed service charge doesn't always reach staff.
local_tip: Tip roughly 10% of the bill in cash directly to the server, even if a service charge already appears on the receipt.
regional_note: Baksheesh culture is especially pronounced in Cairo and tourist-heavy resort areas, where tipping is actively expected for small services beyond just dining.

also_check.note: Tipping isn't local custom and can confuse staff, since good service is already the norm without extra payment.
Tipping 15-20% is expected and forms a real part of server income.
Service is included by law, but leaving a little extra for good service is still a polite gesture.

sources.title: Tipping in Egypt: What to Expect, When to Tip & How Much to Give
